content:
watchOS 27 is coming soon, the next major software update for Apple Watch. I have been testing the watchOS 27 beta all summer, and there are three new features I particularly love.

#1: A New Home Screen View Mode

I think Apple has never really nailed the watchOS home screen. The original honeycomb design looked good in promotional images, and the list view added later is my go-to, but both can feel clumsy to use.

The issue is that Apple Watch is designed for very brief micro-interactions. watchOS comes preloaded with many apps—not to mention third-party additions—and finding the one you want among a large number of apps you never use is really troublesome.

watchOS 27 offers a solution: a Smart App Grid, which is the new default home screen view mode.

The Smart App Grid is similar to the honeycomb-style Grid View, but only shows the five apps you use most often along with the Siri app. In my experience, it consistently shows the apps I want. Occasionally there are exceptions, but you can still open the full app view.

Most of the time, my watch face complications are my primary way of launching apps. But now the Smart App Grid serves as a convenient second option.

#2: Tap Gesture

Over the past few years, Apple has gradually added some new and interesting ways to interact with watchOS through gestures.

First came Double Tap, and last year Wrist Flick was added.

Now watchOS 27 introduces a third option: Tap. It is similar to Double Tap, but is just a single tap, and only works with the Smart Stack.

When browsing the Smart Stack, tap once with your index finger and thumb to select a highlighted widget. Basically it is a handy selection tool.

Now you can open the Smart Stack, browse through it with Double Tap, then use the new Tap gesture to select a widget, and open the relevant app.

#3: Siri AI

Siri AI is the focus of all Apple's new software this fall, and watchOS 27 is no exception.

Apple rebuilt Siri from the ground up for the AI era, a major upgrade compared to before.

watchOS 27 adds a dedicated Siri app, where you can browse your conversation history with the assistant across all devices. Importantly, the Apple Watch version of Siri is not a feature-limited, under-performing wrist version. It is the same Siri AI as on your iPhone, iPad, Mac, and so on.

According to Apple's senior director of watchOS software engineering (via TechRadar), this is one of the goals of the Siri revamp:

Although several other companies have tried to create a successful AI wearable, after the launch of watchOS 27, the already very popular Apple Watch will become one of them.

What are your favorite features of watchOS 27? Let us know in the comments.
